title: To-do
summary: Tasks with lists, due dates, repeats, steps and reminders you can snooze
description:
To-do keeps your tasks on your phone and nowhere else.

**What it does**

- **Today** shows what is due today and what is overdue, in separate sections, with overdue dates in red and one tap to move every overdue task to today.
- **Upcoming** groups planned tasks by day; **Calendar** shows them on a month grid.
- **Inbox** catches everything without a list; make your own lists for work, home, shopping or a trip, each with its own icon and colour.
- Every task can have notes, a due date and time, a priority (high, medium, low), a repeat rule (every weekday, every other Tuesday, the last day of the month) and a checklist of steps.
- Ticking off a repeating task moves it to its next date and clears its steps. You can also skip one round.
- Reminders arrive at the due time, or at a morning time you choose for tasks without a time, with **Done**, **Snooze** and **Tomorrow** buttons right in the notification. If you like, a morning summary at a time you pick tells you what is due today and what is overdue.
- Ticked-off tasks are struck through, then get out of the way but stay in **Completed**, where one tap brings a task back.
- A home-screen widget lists today’s tasks as a checklist, and a second one adds a task in one tap.
- **Progress** shows today as a ring (done out of everything due), the days of this week you finished something and how many tasks, your streak, what is overdue and planned, and the last 14 days as a chart.
- Import and export CSV files: bring your tasks along from the task manager you use today, or keep a backup.
- In English or Slovak, following your phone's language.

**Bring your tasks with you**

Import the CSV file most task apps export: project exports with task, section and priority columns, backup files with list, due date and status columns, task exports from desktop mail clients, or any spreadsheet with a title column. Lists are created as needed, dates in ISO, US or day-first form are read, common repeat rules ("every day", "every Monday", RRULE text) carry over, and anything that cannot be read is kept in the task’s notes.

**What it never does**

No ads, no tracking, no account, no subscription and no internet access: the app cannot reach the network at all. Your tasks stay in this app’s own storage on your phone. Files leave only when you export them to a place you pick.

migration.summary: Imports the CSV files most task managers export: project exports, backup files, desktop mail client task exports and simple spreadsheets with a title column

samples.about: This app’s own export: title, list, due date, time, priority, repeat rule, notes, done
Project export with TYPE, CONTENT, PRIORITY 1 to 4 and recurring words in DATE
Backup file with list names, UTC due dates, RRULE repeats, priority 0 to 5 and status (header line first)
Desktop mail client task export: Subject, US dates, High/Normal/Low priority, Completed status
Spreadsheet saved with semicolons, day-first dates and 24-hour times

research.used_for: An upcoming view grouped by day, with overdue tasks listed first and a way to move them all to a new date at once.
Four priority levels that sort the today and upcoming views; recurring due dates that roll forward to the next occurrence when a task is completed.
Lists plus smart views (today, planned, completed), steps inside a task, reminders and due dates as separate ideas.
Repeat options people expect (daily, weekdays, weekly, monthly, yearly, custom), steps as a checklist, a completed list.
Repeating tasks are set from the date; subtasks; a date is needed before a task can repeat.
Completed tasks are hidden in a collapsible section, can be shown again, and can be deleted in bulk.
Reminder notifications with complete and snooze actions; snoozing for minutes, hours or until tomorrow.
What 1-star reviews complain about: reminders that do not fire, reminders and other basics behind a subscription, recurring-task bugs, clutter; wishes for a calendar view and grouped notifications.

Export format A (project CSV): columns TYPE (task, section, note), CONTENT (title), DESCRIPTION, PRIORITY (1 highest to 4 lowest), INDENT, DATE (date or recurring words such as every day), DEADLINE, comma-separated, UTF-8. Recurring dates lose their start date on export.

Export format B (backup CSV): metadata lines before the header; columns Folder Name, List Name, Title, Content, Due Date (2026-10-20T15:00:00+0000), Repeat (RRULE text), Priority (0, 1, 3, 5), Status (0 open, 1 done, 2 archived), Completed Time, Is All Day.

Export format C (desktop mail client task CSV): Subject, Start Date, Due Date in the locale's date format, Priority (High, Normal, Low), Status (Completed, Not Started), Date Completed, Notes. Column list partly from memory, not verified against a real export.
Export format D (account data export): nested JSON with lists and tasks (title, notes, due, status, completed). Not importable yet.
